source: Tavily web search (advanced depth), retrieved via the Tavily MCP connector. Summaries are written from the search snippets and link to the original page.

solar.title: ITC finds injury from solar imports from India, Indonesia and Laos
solar.summary: The U.S. International Trade Commission's affirmative final vote clears AD/CVD orders on crystalline silicon cells and modules. Commerce is set to issue the orders on November 2, after which CBP collects cash deposits.

solar.title: Commerce publishes final AD and CVD determinations on Indonesian solar cells
solar.summary: Indonesia's final dumping margin rose to 94.36% from 35.15% at the preliminary stage, with countervailing rates of 73.20% to 173.70% depending on the producer.

solar.title: Commerce sets preliminary dumping margins on Indian, Indonesian and Laotian solar cells
solar.summary: Preliminary AD margins: 123.04% for India, 35.15% for Indonesia, 22.46% for Laos. Petitioners had alleged critical circumstances, which can apply duties to entries up to 90 days before the ruling.

solar.title: Preliminary countervailing duties on Indonesian solar cells take effect
solar.summary: Commerce's preliminary CVD determination sets subsidy rates on Indonesian cells and modules, with critical circumstances applied to entries about 90 days earlier.

solar.title: ITC schedules final phase of the India, Indonesia, Laos solar investigations
solar.summary: Covers HTS 8541.42 and 8541.43. A U.S. producers' coalition alleged critical circumstances, citing an import surge ahead of the duties.

aluminum.title: Section 338 tariffs on Canadian goods extended to some Section 232 products
aluminum.summary: 50% Section 338 duties on Canadian goods took effect August 22, 2026, with no USMCA exemption. An updated list effective September 15 adds certain aluminum and steel items, stacking with Section 232 for up to 100% in additional duty.

aluminum.title: UFLPA Entity List expands by 43 companies, including aluminum producers
aluminum.summary: The largest single addition to the list, now 187 entities. The additions span aluminum, apparel, copper, cotton and tomatoes, and many are headquartered outside Xinjiang.

aluminum.title: CBP consolidates forced-labor enforcement guidance for importers
aluminum.summary: Replaces the 2022 UFLPA guidance and lists aluminum among its high-priority sectors, with supply-chain tracing documentation expectations.

cotton.title: UFLPA Entity List reaches 187 entities after cotton and apparel additions
cotton.summary: New designations cover cotton, apparel and downstream products, and many of the companies are outside Xinjiang. The presumption applies to goods made with inputs from listed entities, wherever the goods are sewn.

cotton.title: CBP's 2026 operational guidance adds isotopic-testing guidance for origin checks
cotton.summary: Appendices set out tracing documents for cotton and apparel and cover isotopic testing for origin verification. UFLPA detentions allow 30 days to respond, extendable to 90.

cotton.title: UFLPA detentions in FY2026 track FY2025 levels
cotton.summary: From FY2025 through April of FY2026, CBP detained 17,651 shipments under the UFLPA and denied entry to 10,959. Apparel, footwear and textiles accounted for $9.6 million of detained value.

seafood.title: Commerce narrows the 2025–26 antidumping review of Indian shrimp
seafood.summary: The review was initiated for 393 Indian exporters and is now rescinded for companies with no reviewable entries. The review continues for the rest, under a 2005 order.

seafood.title: Seafood stays on CBP's forced-labor high-priority list
seafood.summary: CBP's consolidated guidance lists seafood among twelve high-priority sectors and points importers to the U.S. Department of Labor's lists of goods produced with forced or child labor.

honey.title: Commerce finds dumping in final review of raw honey from India
honey.summary: Covers June 2023 to May 2024 under the 2022 AD order on raw honey from Argentina, Brazil, India and Vietnam. The decision memo addresses an allegation that honey adulteration created a particular market situation.

honey.title: Preliminary 2024–25 honey reviews published for Argentina, Brazil and Vietnam
honey.summary: Shows the honey orders remain under active annual review across the main competing origins, which matters when trade shifts between them.

gold.title: Reporting questions 'scrap' and 'recycled' gold labels at refineries
gold.summary: Summer 2026 roundup of investigations into how illicitly mined gold can enter legitimate markets when relabeled as scrap or recycled, and into gaps in refinery due diligence.

tin.title: 2025 conflict-minerals filings rely on RMI country-of-origin data dated March 27, 2026
tin.summary: U.S. filers trace 3TG smelters against the Responsible Minerals Initiative's lists. Bolivia appears among possible origins outside the DRC-region covered countries, so it gets lower-risk treatment under Dodd-Frank §1502 reporting.

timber.title: 25% Section 301 tariff on Brazilian goods takes effect
timber.summary: Concludes an investigation that included illegal deforestation among its grounds. The duty applies to Brazilian products not exempted in the notice's annexes. Check whether HS 4407.29 is exempt before reading changes in the trend.

timber.title: USTR finds Brazil's illegal-deforestation practices actionable
timber.summary: Illegal deforestation is one of six practices USTR determined to be unreasonable and burdensome to U.S. commerce.
